name: CRM Foundations
description: Comprehensive CRM operational training enabling sellers to execute the Red Hat sales process within Red Hat Sales Cloud through structured deal management, qualification, account planning, and lifecycle selling workflows.

narratives.name: Accelerating Sales Execution Through CRM Operational Mastery
narratives.description: How structured CRM training transforms seller productivity by embedding sales process discipline into daily platform operations.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise sales organizations deploy CRM platforms to standardize deal execution, yet seller productivity depends on mastering the specific operational workflows, data entry conventions, and integrated tool capabilities that translate process intent into system action. Without structured CRM training, sellers develop inconsistent habits that degrade data quality, slow deal velocity, and reduce the value of analytics investments.

CRM Foundations provides a progressive learning pathway from platform onboarding through advanced capabilities. Sellers learn to create and progress opportunities through stage-gated workflows aligned to the Buyer's Journey, configure quotes using the pricing waterfall, navigate approval and compliance controls, execute agreements through integrated DocuSign CLM, manage account plans with scorecard assessment and whitespace analysis, and leverage embedded customer intelligence from TeleSense and AREN for data-driven engagement decisions.

Sellers who complete CRM Foundations operate with consistent process execution, accurate pipeline data, and proactive account management discipline. Deal velocity increases through streamlined quote-to-cash workflows. Forecasting accuracy improves through disciplined stage management and MEDDPICC qualification. Account growth accelerates through structured planning and intelligence-driven selling. The investment in CRM operational training compounds over time as sellers advance from basic platform proficiency to strategic tool mastery.

narratives.name: Establishing the Commercial Foundation Through Structured CRM Data Entry
narratives.description: How disciplined opportunity creation and configuration in RHSC establishes the data foundation for accurate pipeline management and deal execution.

narrativeContexts.context: Sellers begin each deal by creating an opportunity record in Red Hat Sales Cloud. The quality of initial data entry -- contact roles, partner configuration, close date estimation, and stage assignment -- determines the accuracy of every downstream process from pipeline reporting through approval routing.

The seller must configure the opportunity with complete and accurate commercial context including route-to-market selection, partner role assignment, sales play association, and compliance status assessment, establishing a record that supports both current deal execution and historical analytics.

Opportunity creation starts from the account or contact page using the New Opportunity button. Required fields are populated systematically: primary contact role assignment, estimated close date, initial amount, stage aligned to the Buyer's Journey, and partner configuration for the selected route-to-market. Sales plays and tactics are associated to provide guided engagement content.

A properly configured opportunity provides the foundation for pipeline reporting, forecast accuracy, approval routing, and deal analytics. Partners receive visibility into their deal involvement, compliance teams can assess applicable controls, and managers can evaluate pipeline quality through consistent data entry standards.

narratives.name: Completing the Deal Through Agreement Execution and Order Fulfillment

A validated contract record completes the deal lifecycle, establishing the entitlement foundation for customer success engagement and seeding the renewal opportunity that initiates the next commercial cycle.

patterns.name: CRM Adoption Journey
patterns.description: Progressive pattern coordinating seller CRM proficiency development from platform onboarding through core process execution to advanced analytics and lifecycle selling capabilities.

patternViews.name: Prerequisites
patternViews.description: Seller has RHSC credentials, territory assignment, and CRM Learning Hub access.

narrativeContexts.context: Before beginning CRM adoption, the seller receives Red Hat Sales Cloud access credentials, territory assignment determining account visibility, and access to the CRM Learning Hub containing knowledge base articles, how-to videos, and support resources. These organizational prerequisites establish the foundation for systematic platform learning.

patternViews.name: Platform Foundation
patternViews.description: Seller completes initial workspace setup, understands data hierarchies and access model, and begins basic CRM operations with Guided Help support.

narrativeContexts.context: Platform foundation begins with workspace configuration -- completing the user profile, activating Guided Help (Pendo), personalizing the navigation bar and favorites list, and bookmarking the CRM Learning Hub. The seller validates their understanding of the data access model including territory hierarchy and least privilege principles, and learns to navigate account pages, create contacts, and use smart search to locate records efficiently.

patternViews.name: Core Process Execution
patternViews.description: Seller executes standard deal workflows including opportunity creation, quote configuration, MEDDPICC qualification, relationship mapping, and CRM-native collaboration.

narrativeContexts.context: Core process execution builds seller capability in the standard deal workflows that constitute daily CRM operations. The seller learns to create opportunities from contact pages, configure quotes through the Quote Line Editor with the pricing waterfall, initiate MEDDPICC scorecards for structured qualification, build relationship maps with organizational hierarchy and influence dynamics, and use Chatter, tasks, and notes for team collaboration. These activities represent the operational foundation that every seller must master before advancing to specialized capabilities.

patternViews.name: Deal Completion and Compliance
patternViews.description: Seller navigates approval workflows, executes agreements through DocuSign CLM, completes deal closure with order processing, and manages compliance controls.
activities: Complete Deal Closure and Order Processing

narrativeContexts.context: Deal completion requires navigating multiple compliance checkpoints and integrated tool workflows. The seller learns to submit quotes for NAT and non-NAT approval, manage credit check resolution, coordinate PQI review for government entity transactions, create and execute agreements through DocuSign CLM with correct template selection and legal verbiage, close opportunities with accurate final data, and monitor order fulfillment through Oracle EBS activation and contract generation.

patternViews.name: Advanced Capabilities
patternViews.description: Seller leverages customer intelligence analytics, develops strategic account plans, executes lifecycle selling for renewals, and uses advanced reporting for pipeline management.

narrativeContexts.context: Advanced capabilities represent the seller's transition from process executor to strategic CRM user. Account planning with the six-part scorecard, whitespace analysis, and SMART-goal initiatives enables systematic growth management. TeleSense and AREN analytics provide real-time customer intelligence for data-driven engagement decisions. Lifecycle selling through structured action plans transforms renewal management from reactive contract events into proactive customer engagement. Advanced reporting with Kanban, Split, and Table views enables pipeline analysis and mass update capabilities for efficient sales management.

patternViews.name: Platform Mastery
patternViews.description: Seller achieves CRM operational mastery through sustained practice, intelligence-driven selling, and continuous improvement across all capabilities.

narrativeContexts.context: Platform mastery is achieved when sellers consistently operationalize all CRM capabilities in an integrated workflow -- using intelligence to inform account strategy, strategy to drive opportunity creation, qualification to validate deals, and process discipline to execute transactions with compliance. Mastery is evidenced by sustained high account plan scores, intelligence-driven expansion pipeline, proactive renewal engagement, and efficient reporting practices that compound over time as CRM data quality improves and institutional knowledge accumulates.

patterns.name: Deal Execution Lifecycle
patterns.description: End-to-end pattern coordinating the commercial transaction from opportunity creation through quote configuration, approval, agreement execution, order fulfillment, contract activation, and renewal generation.

patternViews.name: Prerequisites
patternViews.description: Seller has CRM proficiency, contact record exists, and account/territory data is validated.

narrativeContexts.context: Deal execution requires foundational readiness including an established CRM workspace, validated account data hierarchy, correct territory assignment, and an identified customer contact. These prerequisites ensure that the deal record is built on accurate data from the outset, preventing downstream data quality issues that cause approval delays and order triage.

patternViews.name: Deal Scoping
patternViews.description: Opportunity is created with initial qualification, partner configuration, and compliance context assessed.

narrativeContexts.context: Deal scoping translates identified customer needs into structured CRM records with commercial context. The opportunity is created from the contact page with header information, route-to-market, and partner configuration. MEDDPICC qualification begins with initial assessment of Metrics and Economic Buyer. Compliance context is assessed including GOE status, country of order, and applicable regulatory controls.

patternViews.name: Deal Construction
patternViews.description: Quote is configured with products and pricing, qualification deepened with full MEDDPICC assessment, and stakeholders mapped for commercial readiness.

narrativeContexts.context: Deal construction transforms validated opportunity into a formal commercial proposal. The Quote Line Editor is used to add products, apply the pricing waterfall, and configure billing terms. MEDDPICC qualification deepens with all eight dimensions assessed and scored. The relationship map reveals stakeholder dynamics informing the negotiation strategy. The seller's Closing Status and Next Steps log document the evolving commercial context for team visibility.

patternViews.name: Deal Execution
patternViews.description: Approvals obtained through NAT/non-NAT/credit/PQI channels, agreement created and executed in DocuSign CLM, and deal progressed to closure.
activities: Complete Deal Closure and Order Processing

narrativeContexts.context: Deal execution navigates the approval gauntlet -- NAT pricing approval, credit check at Validate completion, PQI review for government entity transactions, and SEAP assessment for subscription compliance. The agreement is created in DocuSign CLM with correct template selection, legal verbiage, and data verification. Upon full execution, the opportunity is closed with verified final data and documented win/loss rationale.

patternViews.name: Contract and Renewal
patternViews.description: Order is fulfilled through Oracle EBS, contract activates with subscription details, and renewal opportunity auto-generates initiating the next commercial cycle.
activities: Complete Deal Closure and Order Processing

narrativeContexts.context: Contract and renewal completes the deal cycle and initiates the next. The OTI team creates the order from the executed agreement, processing it through Oracle EBS from Draft through Activated. The contract auto-generates from the activated order with subscription details, terms, and web login activation. Within 24 hours, products transfer to the auto-generated renewal opportunity, and lifecycle selling begins with the Discover action plan -- transforming deal closure from an endpoint into a transition point for continuous customer engagement.

patterns.name: Account Growth Strategy
patterns.description: Strategic pattern coordinating account assessment, intelligence-driven opportunity identification, initiative execution, and continuous planning refinement for systematic account growth.

patternViews.name: Prerequisites
patternViews.description: Account exists in RHSC with active opportunities or contracts, and seller has Insights and ClosePlan access.

narrativeContexts.context: Account growth strategy requires an established customer relationship with existing commercial engagement. The account has active opportunities or contracts in RHSC, the seller has access to customer intelligence through TeleSense and AREN, and ClosePlan is available for account planning and relationship mapping. These prerequisites ensure that strategic planning is grounded in real customer context rather than speculative engagement.

patternViews.name: Account Assessment
patternViews.description: Analyze account health through six-part scorecard, customer intelligence review, and stakeholder ecosystem mapping.

narrativeContexts.context: Account assessment synthesizes multiple intelligence sources into a structured understanding of the customer's situation. The six-part scorecard evaluates Account Overview, Account Intelligence, Customer's Ecosystem, Key Stakeholders Management, Technical Landscape, and Customer Success dimensions, producing a risk tier classification (High/Medium/Low). TeleSense health indicators reveal product deployment health while AREN propensity scores quantify cross-sell, expansion, and churn risk across product categories. Data integrity is validated to ensure assessment is based on accurate account information.

patternViews.name: Opportunity Identification
patternViews.description: Map whitespace across product families and business units, create initiatives with SMART goals, and convert identified opportunities to pipeline.

narrativeContexts.context: Opportunity identification translates strategic assessment into actionable growth initiatives. Whitespace mapping reveals product deployment patterns across business units with four statuses (Open, Deployed, Competitive, Competitor). Initiatives are created with SMART goals linking to specific product families, success metrics, and customer business owners. Whitespace cells are converted to potential then actual opportunities with account plan linkage preserving the strategic context. MEDDPICC qualification begins on each identified opportunity to validate commercial viability.

patternViews.name: Progress Review
patternViews.description: Monitor initiative progress, review scorecard trends, assess pipeline advancement, and operationalize intelligence for ongoing engagement.

narrativeContexts.context: Progress review validates that account strategy is producing measurable results. The account plan dashboard shows team contribution levels and initiative progress over time. Scorecard scores are compared against prior assessments to identify improvement trends. Pipeline generated from whitespace conversion is tracked through deal stages. Customer intelligence is continuously monitored for changes in usage health or buying propensity that require strategy adjustment. This review discipline creates the evidence foundation for follow-up planning and strategic account discussions with management.

patterns.name: Compliance Orchestration
patterns.description: Cross-cutting pattern coordinating financial, legal, and regulatory compliance controls embedded throughout the deal execution lifecycle from initial assessment through audit-ready closure.

patternViews.name: Prerequisites
patternViews.description: Deal context is established with account, opportunity, and route-to-market determined.

narrativeContexts.context: Compliance orchestration begins when a deal's commercial context establishes the compliance parameters. The account's GOE status, the country of order, the route-to-market, and the deal size collectively determine which compliance controls will apply. Understanding this compliance landscape early prevents surprises during the approval process and enables parallel processing of compliance requirements alongside deal construction.

patternViews.name: Compliance Assessment
patternViews.description: Identify applicable compliance controls based on deal characteristics including GOE status, country of order, RTM, and discount levels.

narrativeContexts.context: The compliance assessment task identifies which controls apply to the specific deal. The seller evaluates whether the account involves a government or state-owned entity (triggering PQI review), determines the country of order (affecting regulatory requirements), assesses the route-to-market (determining credit check applicability), and estimates the discount level (triggering NAT approval tiers). This assessment informs the approval strategy and timeline for the deal.

patternViews.name: Control Execution
patternViews.description: Trigger and process all required compliance checks and approvals including credit check, NAT, PQI, and SEAP.

narrativeContexts.context: Control execution processes all applicable compliance checkpoints concurrently. The credit check auto-triggers at Validate stage completion for applicable RTM configurations with four possible outcomes (Approved, Pending, Rejected, None). NAT approval is submitted for pricing exceptions based on annualized MSRP thresholds. PQI review is automatically appended as the final approval step for qualifying GOE transactions, adding legal terms and Estimated End-user Price. SEAP assessment is initiated where subscription compliance concerns are identified.

patternViews.name: Resolution and Agreement
patternViews.description: Resolve all compliance gates and embed compliance terms into the agreement document through DocuSign CLM.
activities: Complete Deal Closure and Order Processing

narrativeContexts.context: Compliance resolution produces an audit-ready deal record with a complete approval chain, regulatory terms embedded in the executed agreement, and documented evidence supporting every compliance decision. PQI language and EEP automatically carry from the quote into the DocuSign agreement. Credit check approval is documented in the opportunity. SEAP resolution is tracked through opportunity closure. The resulting deal archive provides the compliance evidence that supports both internal audit and external regulatory review.
